title: Verify incomplete coverage metadata in OpenAQ sensor responses
problem: API #404 reports a location sensor-list HTTP 500 when reporting-period metadata is missing. The pinned original SQL functions produce the five reported null fields, which fail the original API response model. This synthetic contract reproduction does not establish deployed frequency or the intended database/API fix.
humanitarian_relevance: OpenAQ supports community access to pollution measurements. Preventing a sensor metadata failure from interrupting data access could aid analysis; no affected humanitarian user, health outcome or realized benefit is established.

evidence.claim: The issue reports a location sensor-list error; a diagnostic comment attributes five response-validation errors to missing logging/averaging values and proposes requiring those values in the database.

At the pinned source revision, Sensor.coverage permits null but Coverage requires non-null numeric/string fields. The original sensor route calls calculate_coverage with reporting periods when a latest value exists. This is static source evidence, not a reproduced server error.

Eight original-model/synthetic FastAPI scenarios passed expected assertions, including HTTP 500 for incomplete coverage and mixed valid/invalid sensors. Seven outputs from two unchanged SQL coverage functions were checked against the original model; two zero-period controls returned SQLSTATE 22012. The original router and deployed schema were not exercised.

code_surface: API 87c060c28f5b484e0e9953d247082f5e678935c9: Coverage/Sensor/SensorsResponse, fetch_sensors and existing sensor smoke tests. Database 0e49c258186372f4af6c5679a4e1ab47157f0158: two calculate_coverage functions in openaqdb/idempotent/util_functions.sql. Current period-column/migration contract remains unresolved.
proposed_change: First verify the failure and intended coverage contract. If accepted, provide a focused regression and agreed handling for missing reporting metadata; do not silently invent intervals, zero coverage, or widen response nullability.
research_next_step: Exercise the original location-sensor router with synthetic database results and locate the current averaging/logging-period schema and ingestion contract. Resolve API fallback versus ingestion/database invariants before preparing a scope inquiry; do not repeat the completed pure-model and SQL probes.
priority_rationale: Air-pollution burden and named OpenAQ community use motivate this research path. Select the unassigned sensor-access report over future SDK cleanup and already-owned Explorer/API fixes. No implementation priority or realized impact is implied.
tests: Eight original-model/synthetic HTTP scenarios pass expected assertions. Two unchanged calculate_coverage functions ran in PostgreSQL 14.18 single-user mode: seven output/model checks and two division-by-zero boundary checks passed. Source integrity verified for 15 API and five database files. Original router, full upstream suite, deployed schema and operational API remain untested.
environment: Isolated Python 3.13.7 environment installed 17 lockfile-hashed wheels without source builds. Original response models use Pydantic 2.11.1 and FastAPI 0.115.12. SQL ran in a fresh temporary PostgreSQL 14.18 cluster in single-user mode. Both probes ran with OS network denial; no listening service, existing database, cloud deployment or operational data request. Full application/test setup remains unresolved.
maintainer: Issue #404 is open and unassigned with one diagnostic comment; its inspected timeline has no linked PR. No Humanifest outreach, confirmed scope, reviewer commitment or follow-up date.
risks: The demonstrated contract failure may need ingestion/database invariants rather than nullable API fields. Public table SQL omits the period columns while historical import SQL defines nullable columns, so deployed constraints cannot be inferred. Actual prevalence, affected users, full regression environment, AI/bot eligibility and complete contribution policy remain unresolved.

A synthetic FastAPI route reproduces HTTP 500 for incomplete and mixed sensor responses. This verifies the contract mechanism, not original routing or deployment.
